title: Mars crater superposition graph: relative-age relations among 83,370 Martian impact craters
description: A directed graph of Martian impact craters in which each edge records that one crater formed after another. Nodes are the 385,049 craters ≥1 km in the Robbins and Hynek (2012) database (2020 release). Edges come from containment (a crater lying entirely inside another crater's rim) and from rim overlap, oriented by rim-arc completeness in the catalog and by rim continuity on MOLA topography. The graph links 83,370 craters through 77,661 relations (73,183 after transitive reduction) with no cycles. The record contains the edge list, the crater table with graph metrics, a GraphML file, pair-level evidence, validation results, and a self-contained HTML explorer that opens in any browser. Version 0.2.0 adds analyses that use the graph to test crater-count ages and to measure crater degradation: interior crater counts and model ages for craters ≥10 km, a test of whether interior crater densities agree with superposition order, a Bayesian sequence model that combines crater counts with superposition order, Monte Carlo cratering simulations of superposition chain depth, and a fit of crater degradation rates. The record adds the outputs of these analyses; the graph itself is unchanged from version 0.1.0.
